questions.question: Explain the relationship between bits and bytes and their significance in computing.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the relationship between bits and bytes and their significance in computing. /
  • [CO1] Answer: (5 marks) total)
  • • Bit: Basic unit of digital information, can be 0 or 1 (1 mark)
  • • Byte: Collection of 8 bits (1 mark)
  • • Relationship: 1 byte = 8 bits (1 mark)
  • • Significance in computing (2 marks)
  • - Bits used for binary representation
  • - Bytes used as fundamental unit for memory storage
  • - Data storage measured in bytes (KB, MB, GB, etc.)
  • - Character encoding (ASCII uses 1 byte per character)

questions.question: Write a C program to reverse a string.

questions.question: Describe the main functions of compilers, interpreters, and assemblers in programming and their roles in code translation.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the main functions of compilers, interpreters, and assemblers in programming and their
  • roles in code translation. / [CO1]
  • Answer: (10 marks) total)
  • Compiler: (3 marks)
  • • Translates entire high-level language program to machine code at once
  • • Creates executable file that can run independently
  • • Faster execution but slower translation
  • • Examples: GCC for C, Turbo C
  • • Error reporting: All errors shown after compilation
  • Interpreter: (3 marks)
  • • Translates and executes program line by line
  • • No separate executable file created
  • • Slower execution but immediate feedback
  • • Examples: Python, JavaScript interpreters
  • • Error reporting: Stops at first error encountered
  • Assembler: (3 marks)
  • • Translates assembly language to machine code
  • • Works with low-level language (mnemonics to binary)
  • • One-to-one mapping between assembly and machine instructions
  • • Examples: NASM, MASM
  • • Produces object code
  • Comparison/Role in code translation: (1 mark)
  • • All serve as translators between human-readable and machine-executable code

questions.question: Explain the syntax and functioning of a 'for' loop in C. Implement a 'for' loop for the following scenario: A mathematics teacher wants to identify Armstrong numbers between 100 and 500 (inclusive).
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the syntax and functioning of a 'for' loop in C. Implement a 'for' loop for the following scenario: / [CO3] Answer: (10 marks) total) Syntax and Functioning: (4 marks) Syntax: for (initialization; condition; increment/decrement) { // body of loop } Explanation:
  • • Initialization: Executed once at the beginning
  • • Condition: Checked before each iteration
  • • Increment/Decrement: Executed after each iteration
  • • Body: Statements executed when condition is true
  • • Flow: initialization → condition check → body → increment → condition check Program Implementation (finding Armstrong numbers between 100-500): (6 marks) Sample code #include #include int main() { int num, sum, temp, digit, count; printf("Armstrong numbers between 100 and 500:\n"); for(num = 100; num <= 500; num++) { temp = num; sum = 0; count = 0; // Count digits while(temp !=
  • 0) { count++; temp = temp / 10; } temp = num; // Calculate sum of digits raised to power of count while(temp != 0) { digit = temp % 10; sum = sum + pow(digit, count); temp = temp / 10; } // Check if Armstrong number if(sum == num) { printf("%d ", num); } } return 0; }
